newsitem.title: USA: Stocks little changed in listless trading.
newsitem.headline: Stocks little changed in listless trading.

text.p: Stocks were listless Thursday as the market was sandwiched between Wednesday's sell-off in technology shares and Friday's key jobs report for January.
At 1 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 8.46 points at 6,755.36 after the previous day's fall of 87 points.
In the broader market, advances led declines by a small margin on moderate volume of 278 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq composite index edged up 0.83 to 1,349.27, and the American Stock Exchange index was off 0.34 at 585.07.

"The markets seem sedated today," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany Corp. "Everyone is trying to get a sense of what the next major move will be. No one believes we'll see the answer before the employment report."
He said, "Most portfolio managers are simply sitting on their hands, waiting for tomorrow's employment report."
The bond market also was subdued, with the yield on the Treasury's 30-year bond holding at Wednesday's close of 6.76 percent.
Among technology shares rising after Wednesday's washout were Cisco Systems, up 1-3/4 at 64-3/4, International Business Machines, up 3/8 at 148-3/4 and Applied Materials, up 3-1/2 at 47-5/8.
But Intel Corp., however, was down 3-1/8 at 154-1/8.

"The techs are the only sector driving the market. They were under pressure yesterday, but people still love them and are trying to buy them today," said Roy Blumberg, chief investment strategist at Josephthal Lyon & Ross.
"The fact that for the most part the techs are higher today is keeping the market from drifting lower still," he said.
First Albany's Johnson said the drop in technology shares was a mixed blessing.

"I was encouraged to see them sell off because they are now moving towards levels that are beginning to look attractive," he said. "The bad news is that they probably have further to go on the downside."
Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments, said that huge intra-day swings in the market, like the one on Wednesday, helped stave off a major correction.

"When you see intraday swings of 150 or 200 points concentrated in the Dow, selling has a tendency to dry up very quickly. That is a safety net," he said. "We are seeing the benefits of that safety net today."
He said the fact that most technology stocks were rebounding was a positive indication of market stability.

"We are seeing another wave of selling in Intel and some in Microsoft and yet it has not spilled over into all of the other high technologies," Cardillo said. "The fact that the market can manage these intraday swings in my opinion represents a lessening of the danger of a major correction."
Retail stocks rose on higher January sales from stores open at least a year. Sears Roebuck was up 1-1/4 at 49-3/4, Wal-Mart Stores Inc. gained 3/8 at 23-5/8 and Kmart Corp. was up 1/4 at 11.
